title: 1. Hook: The Microscopic Bricks of Life
text: Have you ever wondered what makes up a living being? Think of a giant skyscraper. From far away it looks like one massive structure, but up close, it's made of millions of tiny individual bricks. Are our bodies the same? What are our 'bricks' made of?

title: 2. Socratic Thinking: What's inside an onion peel?
text: If you peel a tiny, transparent piece of skin from an onion and look at it under a powerful microscope, what do you think you'd see? Would it be a smooth, solid sheet, or would it look like little organized compartments?

content.title: 3. Discovery: The Honeycomb Pattern
content.description: Looking through Robert Hooke's primitive microscope in 1665, observing the cork cells that looked like little rooms.

title: 4. The Reveal: Meet the Cell
text: Just like a building is made of bricks, all living organisms are made of microscopic compartments called Cells. The word 'Cell' comes from the Latin word 'cellula', which means 'a small room'. They are the fundamental structural and functional unit of life.

content.preview: The fundamental, structural and functional unit of all living organisms.

content.question: Who was the first scientist to observe cells under a microscope in 1665?

title: 6. Reflection: The City Inside You
text: Imagine trying to build a human without these tiny living rooms. Each cell is alive and does its own work, like miniature factories inside you! If someone asked you to explain what a cell is to a 5-year-old, how would you describe it in your own words?

title: 7. Connection: The Foundation of Biology
text: Cells are the foundation of everything we will study in biology. In future chapters, we will learn how groups of cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs form the organ systems that make up our bodies!

content.title: 8. Mastery: The Cell Hunt
content.instructions: Look around your room right now. Name 3 things made of cells and 3 things NOT made of cells. (Hint: Ask yourself, 'Was this thing ever alive?') Discuss your answers with a friend or teacher.
